title: Raise a dicer's pusher, slide the worn blade grid out, slide the new one in to the stop and lower the pusher through it
instruction: Fit the new blue blade grid in the dicer in place of the worn red one.
context: Food preparation workers change a dicer's blade grid when it dulls or for a new cut: raise the pusher, slide the grid out of its channels, slide the new one fully home and lower the pusher, whose fingers pass the grid only when it is square and home (O*NET 35-2021.00 Food Preparation Workers; 35-2014.00 Cooks, Restaurant). The board's 'Clear the bed of a paper cutter, then lower its blade arm until the safety latch catches', 'Change a press to the die that clears its hidden punch' and 'Replace a blade in a quick-release holder and check it is retained' lower a blade or swap a tool; this one adds a cutting insert slid under retaining lips to a back stop, which a nine-finger pusher must then pass through.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights are above the table. Dicer frame (grey printed plastic, fixed to the table): two cheeks, 10.5 x 1 x 8.4 tall, at x 27 to 37.5, y -5.9 to -4.9 and y 4.9 to 5.9; on each inner face a ledge 1.2 wide (x 27 to 36.5, top 6 up) and, over the rear half, a retaining lip (x 32 to 36.5, underside 7.4 up); a back stop across the rear at x 36.5 to 37.5; a hinge pedestal 5 tall at x 27.5 to 36.5, y -11.5 to -5.9. Pusher (150 g): hinged on an axis along x at y -10.5, 6.5 up, turning from down to a back stop 109 degrees up (1.9 rad, past vertical). Down, its white aluminium block, 9 x 9 x 1.2, lies at x 27.5 to 36.5, y -4.5 to 4.5, 8.7 to 9.9 up, with nine grey fingers, 1.2 x 1.2 x 3.2 long, reaching down to 5.5 up at x 29.3, 32 and 34.7, y -2.7, 0 and 2.7; two grey arms 2 wide join the block to the hinge; an orange handle, 3 (x) x 1.8 (y) x 3.5 tall, stands on the block at x 30.5 to 33.5, y 2.7 to 4.5. Two blade grids (printed plastic, 80 g each): a frame 9 x 9 x 1 with a 0.6 border and two 0.3 blades each way, leaving nine 2.4 openings; on its front edge a handle plate 2.6 (x) x 5 (y) x 1 carrying an upright grip tab 1.8 (x) x 3 (y) x 3 tall. Worn grid: red with a yellow tab, home in the dicer, frame at x 27.5 to 36.5, y -4.5 to 4.5, on the ledges and against the back stop, tab at x 26.1, y 0, with the pusher down through it. New grid: blue with a green tab, lying flat on a grey plastic stand (12 x 10 x 2 tall, centred at x 23, y 17), frame centred at x 24.5, y 17, tab toward the arms at x 18.6. Drain board: dark grey plastic, 12 x 12 x 1 tall, centred at x 21, y -18. Fits: a grid has 4 mm a side between the cheeks and 4 mm under the lips; the fingers have 6 mm a side in the openings.
scoring: At the end, open both grippers; measure with a ruler and a top-down photo. Home (H): the blue grid on both ledges between the cheeks, rear face within 3 mm of the back stop, tilted at most 3 degrees (5 mm end to end). Down (D): the pusher within 0.05 rad of fully down (middle of its block within 5 mm of its down height, 8.7 cm). Up: the pusher 1.5 rad or more from down (leaning back past vertical). Out (O): the red grid wholly outside the dicer, flat on the drain board: underside within 4 mm of the board's top, tilted at most 5 degrees (8 mm end to end), frame middle over the board. 1.0: H, D and O. 0.5: H and O, pusher up. 0.25: O, pusher up, blue grid not home. Otherwise 0, including a pusher resting on the blades or let go part way, a red grid on the table, leaning or off the table, and a grid held more than 1 cm above every support.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Raise the pusher, slide the red grid back home against the stop and lower the pusher through it; put the blue grid back on its stand with its tab toward the arms.
fidelity: Approximate. The frame, grids and pusher are rigid boxes with no sharp edges and no food. The hinge is a damped joint with hard stops at 0 and 1.9 rad; the pusher collides with the grids and the arms but not with its own frame. A grid 1 cm short of home stops the pusher 0.2 rad up. The simulator scores the final step without opening the grippers, so a grid held more than 1 cm above every support counts as not placed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (left arm reached to the blue grid on its stand, red grid stayed put); demo: 1.0 (right arm slid red grid onto drain board, left arm fitted blue grid, pusher lowered)
